counterfactual.change: Reduced body1 vx from -47.87 to -10 (single field change). Same mass ratio and dt, same steps. Collision still occurs but energy stays conserved (~694 J) and no rule violated, proving impulse bug is triggered by high relative speed.

explanation: Energy jumps from ~1790 J to 23888 J at the first collision (step 6->7) between a heavy static body (m=16.9) and a light fast body (m=1, vx=-47.8). The heavy body gains speed 0.84->51.2 m/s, larger than the impactor, while the light body keeps ~45 m/s. This violates momentum conservation and creates energy; impulse calculation likely swaps masses or scales by 1/m incorrectly, amplified at high relative speed and high mass ratio.
vision_note: A small blue circle on the right closes in on a larger blue circle on the left from step 4 to 6, and at step 7 they make contact with slight overlap. No post-collision explosion is visible in these frames, but step 7 clearly marks the first impact between the light fast body and the heavy body where the energy violation occurs.
